A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VideoITG work. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, and the methods, equations, tables and figures can be matched despite extensive reformatting and relocation.

before.justification: V1 reports original VideoITG benchmark results and ablations in Section 5, plus inference timings and annotation-quality IoU results in the appendix.

after.justification: V2 retains original benchmark, ablation, timing and annotation-quality results, and adds comparisons with other selectors and evaluations using additional answering models.

M1.justification: The three-stage VidThinker pipeline, four instruction types, VideoITG variants A-C and Algorithm 1 are retained. The added CLIP-sampling explanation describes an existing algorithm. The multi-resolution configuration is introduced as a comparison setting, without a documented revision to the core selection algorithm.

E1.justification: The training sources, VideoITG-40K dataset and main and supplementary QA benchmark coverage are retained. Added experiments vary answering models and frame budgets. The CG-Bench heading becomes CG-Bench-mini with unchanged matched scores; this does not establish new task or domain coverage.

E2.justification: V2 Table 2 adds comparisons with BOLT, Frame-VOYAGER, Q-Frame, AKS, QuoTA and Gen-S. V1's SigLIP and standalone InternVL2.5-8B scoring comparison disappears. The broad benchmark comparison, moved from v1 Table 3 to v2 Table 6, removes GPT-4o and Gemini-1.5-Flash/Pro rows and replaces Qwen2-VL-7B with Qwen2.5-VL-7B.

E3.justification: V2 substantially expands evaluation configurations through additional answering models, smaller frame budgets and a multi-resolution comparison with Q-Frame (Tables 2-3 and Figure 1). Existing training settings remain stable. The exact Q-Frame comparison allocation is unresolved: Table 2's caption specifies 4+8+32 frames, while its rows specify 8+16+32.

E4.justification: Figure 1 extends frame-budget sensitivity analysis to smaller budgets and competing selectors. V1 Section 5.4's comparison probing different scoring mechanisms is removed. The architecture, annotation-stage and pretraining ablations retain their original individual scores, and the qualitative case studies and annotation-quality analysis remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run counts, random-seed information, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The additional results follow the same reporting practice.

E6.justification: V2 adds substantial selector and backbone results; for example, Table 3 newly reports Qwen3-VL averages of 59.2 with uniform sampling and 65.8 with VideoITG. Most matched older results remain unchanged. The 64-frame LLaVA-Video entry reports 56.1 for VideoMME-Long versus 57.0 in v1. Removed comparison rows and 64-frame CG-Bench entries also change the reported evidence; differing table averages should not be treated as performance gains.

T1.justification: Equations 1-7 retain the same annotation mappings, inference pipeline and anchor-averaging definition. Algorithm 1 is unchanged apart from formatting. No new formal assumptions, theorems, proofs or substantive derivations are introduced.

C1.justification: The dataset, model and general performance contributions remain. The introduction replaces its original benchmark-gain summary with an explicit efficiency claim: 16 VideoITG frames match 64 uniformly sampled frames on VideoMME. V2 also strengthens the dataset-quality claim to more than fourfold improvement without adding corresponding quality evidence.

C2.justification: V2 removes the explicit limitation concerning separately trained selection and answering modules, along with the discussion of multi-turn KV-cache tradeoffs. It adds an explanation linking limited LongVideoBench gains to text-referencing tasks and notes low-resolution recognition limitations. The principal interpretations of the architecture and pretraining ablations remain.

D1.justification: V2 Section 5.3 specifies how the existing annotation ablations operate: direct visual prediction of temporal boundaries without clip captioning, and training on all frame indices inside coarse boundaries without frame localization. Appendix C.3 explains the retained sampling algorithm. These are documentation additions; the PDFs do not establish changes to those experiments. Existing hyperparameters, hardware disclosures and project access remain.

R1.justification: Related work adds a focused keyframe-selection discussion covering query-guided, adaptive and multi-resolution approaches, including new references to BOLT, QuoTA, AKS, Gen-S and Q-Frame. This substantially expands positioning against closely related selectors beyond v1's broad Video-LLM and temporal-grounding discussion. Frame-Voyager was already cited in v1 and is not a newly introduced work.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, model descriptions and results narrative are extensively rewritten and reorganized. V2 adds an LLM-use appendix and sampling-algorithm explanation, removes the separate scoring-method ablation section and limitations paragraph, and moves the broad benchmark comparison into the appendix.

P2.justification: V2 changes the document to a two-column layout and substantially reflows figures, tables and appendices. It adds the frame-budget plot, introduces a larger selector-comparison table, embeds improvements within result cells and adds an ablation-average column. The broad benchmark table is relocated and reformatted; existing diagrams and qualitative examples are retained and renumbered.

improvement.justification: The direct comparisons with specialized selectors and results on recent answering models strengthen evidence beyond v1's narrower evaluation. The net gain is limited by removed training/cache caveats and new reporting problems: Q-Frame's frame allocation conflicts between caption and rows, its score is 57.6 in Section 5.2 versus 59.7 in Table 2, and the new fourfold instruction-quality claim lacks supporting evidence.
